dunrobin_guide.text: Welcome to Dunrobin. One hundred and eighty-nine rooms, which makes it the biggest house in the northern Highlands. We don't clean them all on the same day.
The oldest part is a medieval keep, buried inside the Victorian bits like a stone inside a peach. The spires were added in the 1840s by Sir Charles Barry, who went on to the Houses of Parliament.
The family also had the Highland Clearances done in their name, and we don't hide that. The museum and the memorials up the coast tell the story of the people who were put out.

dunrobin_falconer.text: The falconry displays run in the gardens most days in summer. Hawks, falcons, owls. The peregrine stoops faster than anything else alive.
The trick is never to look the bird in the eye while it's eating. Same with my brother.
